From 22b89ba178dd0a66a26699ead014a3e73ff8e044 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sandipan Das <sandipan@linux.ibm.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2021 13:37:44 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/sstep: Fix darn emulation

Commit 8813ff49607e ("powerpc/sstep: Check instruction validity
against ISA version before emulation") introduced a proper way to skip
unknown instructions. This makes sure that the same is used for the
darn instruction when the range selection bits have a reserved value.

Fixes: a23987ef267a ("powerpc: sstep: Add support for darn instruction")
Signed-off-by: Sandipan Das <sandipan@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210204080744.135785-2-sandipan@linux.ibm.com

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c b/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c
index 11f14b209d7f..683f7c20f74b 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c
@@ -1916,7 +1916,7 @@ int analyse_instr(struct instruction_op *op, const struct pt_regs *regs,
 				goto compute_done;
 			}
 
-			return -1;
+			goto unknown_opcode;
 #ifdef __powerpc64__
 		case 777:	/* modsd */
 			if (!cpu_has_feature(CPU_FTR_ARCH_300))
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c`**
   - The line `return -1;` was replaced with `goto unknown_opcode;`. This change alters the flow of the function to handle unknown opcodes by redirecting to a label (`unknown_opcode`) instead of returning an error code directly.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `sstep.c` is related to the previous commit (8813ff49607e) that introduced a mechanism to skip unknown instructions based on the ISA version. The current patch enhances this mechanism specifically for the "darn" instruction by ensuring that when a reserved value is encountered in the range selection bits, the instruction is properly handled by redirecting to the `unknown_opcode` label rather than returning an error. This ensures consistency in how unknown instructions are processed, aligning with the intended behavior established in the earlier commit.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
case 19:
    switch ((word >> 1) & 0x3ff) {
        ...
        default:
            op->type = UNKNOWN;
            return 0;
```
Reason:
The code incorrectly sets the instruction type to `UNKNOWN` and returns `0` for the "darn" instruction when the range selection bits have a reserved value. This behavior does not align with the intended error handling mechanism, which should skip unknown instructions based on the ISA version.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
case 19:
    switch ((word >> 1) & 0x3ff) {
        ...
        default:
            goto unknown_opcode;
```
Reason:
The fix redirects the flow to the `unknown_opcode` label instead of setting the instruction type to `UNKNOWN` and returning `0`. This ensures that the proper error handling mechanism is invoked, allowing the system to skip the unknown instruction correctly based on the ISA version.
